title: iter-2 LOC ballooned to 1211 (4-6x spec envelope of 200-300)
description: Total LOC across the nine TS/TSX files plus vite.config.ts is now 1211 (wc -l). Iter-1 was 603, the spec envelope is 200-300 for a single-route React + Vite read-only SPA. dataLayer.ts alone grew from ~80 to 413 lines. While the CR-1 fix (real chain traversal) genuinely earns most of the new code (Pool->Versioned->PoolInner->BigVector slice walking is real work documented in chain-shape.md), the App.tsx polling effect duplicates ~30 LOC of cards-mapping logic from the initial-load effect, and the dataLayer carries a parallel (now unused-in-prod) public API. The deliverable is now ~4x the spec budget; previous iter-1 finding R4-012 flagged 2x.
impact: Maintenance surface tripled in two iterations against a fixed contract. New file boundaries blur (dataLayer.ts mixes JSON-RPC envelope, traversal, pagination, event parsing, AND business composition in one 413-line module). When a future cycle changes any one concern, the blast radius is the whole file.
recommendation: Split dataLayer.ts into rpc.ts (JSON-RPC envelope), poolReader.ts (resolvePoolInnerFields + traverseBigVector + buildPoolInnerState), eventReader.ts (buildQueryEventsFn), and a small composer (fetchPoolStats + runDataLayer). Hoist the cards-fallback mapping out of App.tsx's two effects into a single helper. Document the LOC overshoot in the consolidated review with an explicit sign-off if the chain-traversal complexity is judged unavoidable.
evidence: wc -l src/*.ts src/*.tsx src/components/*.tsx vite.config.ts -> 1211 total

title: types.ts exports 5 unused interfaces — partial fix to iter-1 R4-001
description: Iter-2 fixed R4-001 partially: PoolDescriptor, LoadedManifest, PoolInnerState, Order, Book are now imported from types.ts. But 5 of the 9 exported interfaces remain entirely unused across src/ and tests/: ManifestPoolEntry, DeploymentManifest, BigVectorMeta, RawFillEntry, RawOrderInfoEvent. Grep for each across src/ and tests/ returns zero importers; the only references are inside types.ts itself or in doc comments. Worse, the types.ts header explicitly claims to be the home for `PoolCardData`, but PoolCardData is still declared in components/PoolCard.tsx (lines 11-25) and never moved.
impact: The single-source-of-truth narrative the file's doc comment promises is false. A maintainer who reads the comment will believe types.ts is canonical for PoolCardData and edit it there — to no effect. Five dead exports add visual noise (~50 LOC) and invite the next maintainer to wire them up to something rather than delete them.
recommendation: Either (a) delete the 5 unused interfaces from types.ts, OR (b) actually use them: type RunDataLayerArgs.manifest as DeploymentManifest, type the JSON-RPC parsedJson in dataLayer's buildQueryEventsFn as RawOrderInfoEvent / RawFillEntry, type the BigVectorMeta extraction in buildPoolInnerState. Move SparklinePoint and PoolCardData into types.ts to honor the header comment OR retract the claim from the comment.

title: main.tsx mutates deps.loadManifest after construction — closure-over-let smell
description: main.tsx defines `deps` with the original `loadManifest`, then four lines later reassigns `deps.loadManifest` to a wrapper that captures the original via `_origLoadManifest` and side-effects a `let cachedPackageId = ''` on every load. The wrapper-after-construction pattern is needed only because `fetchPoolStats` is defined inside the same `deps` object literal and needs the packageId that loadManifest produces. The result is a load-order trap (App must call deps.loadManifest before any deps.fetchPoolStats, otherwise packageId is empty string) and a module-mutable variable that drift-tests cannot observe.
impact: Subtle correctness landmine for the next maintainer who calls fetchPoolStats outside the App's known order, but the simplicity smell is the bigger issue: the construction goes (a) declare deps, (b) declare let cachedPackageId, (c) save deps.loadManifest, (d) reassign deps.loadManifest with a closure that captures the let. Reading the code requires three passes to follow.
recommendation: Build a single object after computing both halves: `const cachedManifestPromise = await loadAndParse(); deps = { loadManifest: () => cachedManifestPromise, fetchPoolStats: (d) => fetchSinglePoolStats(RPC_URL, (await cachedManifestPromise).deepbookPackageId, d, Date.now()) }`. Or better: refactor App.tsx so fetchPoolStats accepts the LoadedManifest as a second arg, eliminating the need to thread packageId via module state.

title: RawFillEvent and FillRecord are structurally identical — pointless 1:1 mapping
description: fillFetcher.ts exports `RawFillEvent { poolId, timestampMs, baseQuantity, price }`. fillAggregator.ts exports `FillRecord { poolId, timestampMs, baseQuantity, price }`. Same four fields, same string vs number types. dataLayer.ts:349 maps one to the other field-for-field with `rawFills.map((f) => ({ poolId: f.poolId, timestampMs: f.timestampMs, baseQuantity: f.baseQuantity, price: f.price }))` — a copy that produces an identical object. Two type names for one shape, plus a runtime allocation that does nothing.
impact: The reader has to verify the two interfaces actually match (they do, today) and that the map is not silently dropping fields (it isn't). Pure noise; if the shape ever drifts on one side and not the other, the structural cast becomes a hidden bug that the type system used to catch.
recommendation: Pick one — either re-export RawFillEvent as FillRecord from fillAggregator.ts, or have fillFetcher.ts return FillRecord[] directly. Drop the .map(). If the two are intended to diverge later, document the planned divergence in a comment.

title: App.tsx duplicates ~30 LOC of cards-mapping logic across two effects
description: The initial-load useEffect (lines 44-82) and the periodic-refresh useEffect (lines 91-125) both: (a) call Promise.allSettled over fetchPoolStats, (b) build cards via the same .map with sentinel-card fallback, (c) build poolErrors with the same filter+map, (d) setState with status:'ready'. The two blocks differ only in where they get the pool list from (manifest.pools vs manifestPoolsRef.current). ~30 LOC are mechanically duplicated.
impact: Any change to the sentinel-card shape, error-collection logic, or status semantics has to be made in two places and they will silently diverge. The H-5 polling fix added complexity that should have been factored into the H-4 fix.
recommendation: Extract `async function refreshCards(pools, deps): Promise<{cards, poolErrors}>` and call it from both effects. Or better: collapse to a single effect that runs once on mount, then re-runs every REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS via a guarded interval — single state machine, one set of mapping logic.

title: Two parallel public APIs in dataLayer: runDataLayer (test-only) and fetchSinglePoolStats (prod-only)
description: dataLayer.ts exports BOTH `runDataLayer(args)` and `fetchSinglePoolStats` (line 413: `export { fetchPoolStats as fetchSinglePoolStats }`). main.tsx uses fetchSinglePoolStats per-pool (because App.tsx orchestrates the per-pool dispatch and packageId caching). Only networkShape.test.ts uses runDataLayer (to lock down the outbound HTTP set). The runDataLayer wrapper has its own Promise.allSettled, its own descriptor mapping, and its own sentinel-card construction — all logic that the production path (App.tsx) re-implements.
impact: Two flows do nearly the same thing with different orchestration. If a per-pool guarantee changes (e.g. sentinel card adds a field, error handling changes), three sites update. The test-only runDataLayer is itself a tautology risk: networkShape.test.ts could pass even if the production path were broken, because the test never exercises App.tsx.
recommendation: Pick one orchestrator. Either (a) delete fetchSinglePoolStats and have App.tsx call runDataLayer once per refresh (returns PoolCardData[] in manifest order), or (b) delete runDataLayer and have networkShape.test.ts call fetchSinglePoolStats directly in a loop. Option (a) is cleaner: the test then exercises the same code path the user does.
evidence:
export async function runDataLayer(args: RunDataLayerArgs): Promise<PoolCardData[]> { ... Promise.allSettled ... sentinel cards ... }
export { fetchPoolStats as fetchSinglePoolStats };

title: decodeBidPrice intentionally retained as wrong-against-prod fallback for tests
description: marketStats.ts:40-44 retains `decodeBidPrice(orderId)` whose comment in dataLayer.ts:CR-2 and types.ts:64-66 explicitly states the bid order_id bit-decode is wrong against real chain order_ids — Order.price is now injected from OrderInfo events as the preferred path. The fallback exists solely so existing tests that build Order fixtures via `encodeBid(price)` (round-tripping their own bit math) continue to pass. The comment at marketStats.ts:53-54 admits this: `the order_id decode is tautologically correct against test fixtures but wrong against real chain order_ids`.
impact: A code path the runtime never takes (because Order.price is always injected by the data layer in prod) is kept alive only to satisfy tests that exercise their own encoding inverse. This is the textbook tests-vs-impl tautology pattern bleeding into simplicity: ~10 LOC of dead-on-prod code that future maintainers will assume is load-bearing.
recommendation: Either (a) delete decodeBidPrice entirely and update the test fixtures to provide Order.price directly (matches what the runtime actually does), OR (b) if test-only encoding is genuinely useful for round-trip property tests, move decodeBidPrice into a tests/_helpers file and import it from there. The production path should not contain code its own author labels as wrong.

title: rpcId mutable module-counter survives iter-2 — iter-1 R4-006 not addressed
description: Iter-1 R4-006 flagged `let rpcId = 0;` at module scope as needless global mutable state for a JSON-RPC id that doesn't need cross-call uniqueness. Iter-2 made the issue worse: dataLayer.ts now issues many more RPC calls per page-load (sui_getObject + suix_getDynamicFields per pool, plus per slice + per inner-field traversal + per fill page), and every one of them increments the same module counter. The counter leaks across React re-renders, polling intervals, and test runs in the same process.
impact: Tiny in practice — Sui RPC does not enforce id uniqueness. Still: 'production-flavored' state in a module that does no other module-state work, and counter values across the test suite are now nondeterministic in a way that some snapshot test could later trip on.
recommendation: Replace with `id: 1` (Sui RPC does not need correlation here) or scope the counter inside `runDataLayer` / `fetchPoolStats` so it resets per orchestration call.

title: RunDataLayerArgs.manifest still typed inline instead of using DeploymentManifest
description: Iter-1 R4-005 flagged the inline `manifest: { network?; packages?; pools? }` shape as a slightly-different copy of DeploymentManifest. Iter-2 added DeploymentManifest to types.ts (line 30) — and then did not import it in dataLayer.ts. RunDataLayerArgs.manifest is still declared with the same inline shape it had in iter-1.
impact: Three nearly-identical manifest shapes still exist (DeploymentManifest in types.ts, the inline RunDataLayerArgs.manifest, and the RawManifest local in manifest.ts:28). Each accepts inputs the others would reject; the contract is now whatever the loosest of the three is. Visible to anyone wiring a non-test caller of runDataLayer.
recommendation: `import type { DeploymentManifest } from './types.js'` at the top of dataLayer.ts and replace the inline shape with `manifest: DeploymentManifest`. Also: `RawManifest` in manifest.ts:28 can be replaced by `Partial<DeploymentManifest>` or just `unknown` (parseManifest already validates).

title: Vite middleware is appropriately small — confirms no over-engineering of CR-3
description: Reviewing CR-3 specifically: the middleware is 22 lines, reads the file fresh on each request (no caching, which is correct for dev), returns 404 with an actionable error message on miss, and is gated to GET /localnet.json only. No over-abstraction (no plugin wrapper, no factory, no env-driven path). This is the right scope for a dev-only manifest passthrough.
impact: Positive — confirms one of the iter-2 additions did not blow up the simplicity budget. Flag as info so the consolidator can credit the vite config when assessing the LOC overshoot in R4-001.
recommendation: No action. Optionally: read MANIFEST_DISK_PATH from an env var fallback if the sandbox is ever moved out of ~/workspace/, but contract pins the path so this is not needed.

title: Order.price? injection adds a defensible but optional indirection
description: Order.price is declared optional (`price?: number`) so the data layer can populate it from OrderInfo event and computeMarketStats can prefer it. The optional shape is defensible because: (a) chain-shape.md confirms price is NOT on the chain Order struct; (b) tests that round-trip via order_id decode want to omit price. The smell would be making it required and forcing test fixtures to fake prices, which would create a different tautology.
impact: Net-neutral. The optionality is honest about the actual data shape (chain vs event-companion). Flagging as info because the existence of two price sources is itself the underlying complexity, but that complexity belongs to the chain, not to the code.
recommendation: Keep as-is. Optional follow-up: add a guard that bestAsk/bestBid are NOT computed if any Order in the book lacks .price, since the order_id fallback is wrong against real chain data per the comments. Without the guard, prod can silently fall through to the wrong-but-test-passing branch.

title: App.tsx polling interval re-renders cards but never re-loads the manifest
description: REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 20_000 satisfies the 30s freshness AC for sparkline updates, but the polling effect only re-fetches per-pool stats — the manifest is loaded exactly once. If the sandbox is restarted with a new pool added mid-session, the dashboard never picks it up. Spec AC1.2 reads 'the displayed pool set matches whatever the sandbox most recently published' which is ambiguous about runtime adds. Likely out of scope, but worth a one-line note.
impact: Edge case only — sandbox restarts mid-session are an explicit decision-gate concern (G-Boot says 'a sandbox restart mid-cycle requires re-checking'). The page would happily display stale pools with sentinels until refreshed.
recommendation: Either (a) acknowledge in a comment that the manifest is load-once and document that sandbox restart requires a page reload, or (b) re-fetch the manifest inside the polling effect alongside the per-pool stats. Option (a) is the lower-LOC choice and matches the read-only single-route SPA simplicity envelope.
evidence:
manifestPoolsRef.current = manifest.pools;
// (only set inside the initial-load effect, never updated by the polling effect)
